claims.claim_vi: The source maps email to postal mail and names MUA, MTA (SMTP) and MDA, with POP3 or IMAP for retrieval.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source expands MTA as 'mail transmission agent'; the SMTP standard names it Mail Transfer Agent, which the lesson uses.
claims.verified_by: Terminology from RFC 5321; Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only).

claims.claim_vi: The sender's MTA finds the receiving MTA through the recipient domain's MX record, falling back to the domain's address record when there is none (RFC 5321 section 5.1).
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only).

claims.claim_vi: RFC 5321 section 4.5.4.1: an MTA queues mail it cannot deliver and retries; retry interval at least 30 minutes, give-up time generally at least 4 to 5 days.
claims.verified_by: Retry and give-up wording matched against an RFC 1123/5321 quotation returned by a web search on 2026-10-19; the RFC page itself was not opened.

design_notes_vi: Khung một là bốn vai nối nhau; khung hai là ba ghi chú (giao thức, MX, hàng đợi).
source_deviations: The source's postal analogy (mailbox, post office) is dropped.
The lesson adds MX lookup and queueing/retry, which the source does not mention.
MTA is spelled Mail Transfer Agent, not 'mail transmission agent' as in the source.
